answer: Each agent earns voting weight by locking a bond in a shared vault and completing randomly assigned tasks that other agents can verify. Surprise audits check the work; a failed check forfeits the bond and removes the agent’s accrued weight. To create many useful identities, an attacker must fund each one and sustain verified activity over time, rather than simply echo claims from fresh accounts. A lagoon of dormant aliases still ties up capital and risks seizure.
